llm.summary: The skill is a disclosed VMware audit and policy helper that stores local audit data and rules, with no artifact evidence of hidden execution, exfiltration, or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: Bash access is used for installation and vmware-audit CLI workflows, and local files are under ~/.vmware or OPS_HOME. The skill documents read-only agent detection by environment-variable presence and states that it does not make network connections or send webhook data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a pinned uv package, vmware-policy==1.18.1, and the artifact contains Markdown documentation rather than bundled executable scripts. The external package code itself was not present in the workspace for code-level review.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are scoped to audit-log queries, policy-rule management, and integration with the VMware skill family; routing guidance points other VMware tasks to other skills.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent local audit.db, rules.yaml, and undo.db state is expected for audit and policy behavior, is disclosed, and is permission-restricted best-effort. The VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED escape hatch and best-effort audit writes are disclosed operational risks rather than hidden persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, audit logging, optional policy rules, sanitization, and a CLI/library used by VMware skills, matches the documented capabilities. Users should note that the packaged default policy denies nothing until they configure rules.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want a local VMware-skill audit and policy layer. Protect ~/.vmware because audit rows can include infrastructure names, parameters, results, and errors; configure rules.yaml if you expect policy blocking; do not leave VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 set in the MCP host environment; and review the pinned vmware-policy package source if supply-chain assurance is required.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: The kubeconfig/token references describe redaction behavior for sensitive return values and audit rows, not instructions to read credential stores.
[SQP-1] expected: The activation language is broad because this is an infrastructure dependency, but the skill is marked user-invocable false and its documented scope is audit and policy handling for VMware skills.
[PE2] expected: The chmod examples set restrictive permissions on ~/.vmware and audit.db; they do not use sudo or request elevated privileges.
[RA2] expected: The local ~/.vmware files are disclosed audit and policy state, with no cron, service, startup hook, or backdoor persistence shown in the artifacts.
[RA2] expected: Best-effort audit persistence is a real limitation because tool calls can proceed if audit writes fail, but it is explicitly documented and does not show deceptive or unauthorized persistence.
[EA2] expected: The cited text discusses policy rules and routing to vmware-pilot for enforced approval; this skill does not itself auto-execute high-impact VMware actions.
[E3] expected: The filesystem command checks the specific ~/.vmware/rules.yaml file mtime for troubleshooting and is not broad local enumeration or exfiltration.
